We are thrilled to highlight Destiny Washington, an inspiring member of the Urban League of Greater Chattanooga's Young Professionals Institute! As part of the 4th cohort of the National Urban League’s Education Fellowship, Destiny spent 6 impactful months exploring school choice and alternative pathways to enhance education in Black and Urban communities.
 One of the standout moments of her journey was visiting Black-owned independent schools in Jackson, Mississippi, including the historic Piney Woods School. This experience fueled Destiny’s passion for creating change, leading her to host an interactive civics and choice learning lab for youth ages 11-17. 
 Through this initiative, she introduced vital civic education and school choice policies to empower young minds and their families. Destiny’s dedication culminated in a powerful presentation at the NUL conference, showcasing the importance of early exposure and intentional development for students in Hamilton County.
 Join us in celebrating Destiny’s commitment to education and her role in shaping a brighter future for our community! 🌍✨ #UrbanLeague #YoungProfessionals #CommunityImpact #EducationForAll #DestinyWashington

If you've been following the news recently, you may have noticed the high level of immigration agent activity in Tennessee and across the country. In response, La Paz has relaunched our Latinx Community Relief Fund to support families affected by detentions and deportations.💚
 Our Latinx Community Relief Fund is an emergency fund that offers financial assistance to Latino families who lack resources and find themselves in difficult situations. Since January 2025, we have provided thousands of dollars in rental assistance and government services through service, but our funds are running out. This summer we set the goal of raising $10,000 dollars to continue helping Latino families in these difficult times.💚
 Do you want to give your grain of sand and support the local Latino community? You can get involved in several ways! You can donate directly to the Latinx Community Relief Fund, where every dollar you donate directly supports members of the community. Also, you can invest your time and volunteer with us, connecting with Latino families and helping our team. You can learn more about the Relief Fund and different ways you can get involved by visiting our website lapazchattanooga.org/alivio 🔗

items.title: Arts organizations that are small in stature but big in addressing community cultural needs are facing economic pressure...
items.content_text:
Arts organizations that are small in stature but big in addressing community cultural needs are facing economic pressures.
 According to national data from 2024, arts nonprofits' revenues have not kept pace with inflation, while support from individual foundations, corporations and the public has declined. Meanwhile, recent cuts and pushback from the Trump administration have also had an impact.
 Jeffrey Brown reports for our Art in Action series, which explores the intersection of art and democracy, as part of our CANVAS coverage.

This summer, we celebrated the one-year mark of our Impact Cohort!
 This three-year collaborative, fueled by a $6.6 million investment from United Way, is made up of 19 all-star local nonprofits. By sharing resources, learnings, and expertise, this group uses each other's distinctive strengths to amplify our shared work: building an ecosystem of support in our community, and especially for our local ALICE families.
 In just one year, collaboration has already led to exciting new initiatives. The YMCA and Crabtree Farms are helping bring fresh food to families throughout the summer. The Chattanooga Area Food Bank and Signal Centers are creating workforce pathways, while Chattanooga 2.0 and Chattanooga Neighborhood Enterprise are strengthening family engagement in Alton Park. And this just skims the surface.
 Learn more about the Impact Cohort and the powerful ways they're collaborating to strengthen Chattanooga at https://hubs.la/Q04rvKCR0.

We would like to congratulate Captain David Tallent on his retirement from the Chattanooga Fire Department after 26 years of service!
 Captain Tallent’s career has been defined by forward-thinking leadership and technical excellence. Through the years, he has been integral in some of our department's most critical specialized programs, spearheading the creation of our Urban Search & Rescue (USAR) team and our regional hazmat response capabilities.
 His tactical expertise was proven time and again during his tenure on our rescue squads and within the Special Operations Division. Furthermore, his commitment to the future of our department was solidified during his time in our Training Division, where he mentored and trained countless firefighters.
 Thanks to Captain Tallent for his many years of service to Chattanooga. We wish him a long, healthy, and happy retirement!

items.content_text:
📍 A Great First Step for Downtown Red Bank!
 On Friday, July 31, the Tennessee Downtowns Steering Committee held its first official meeting, marking an exciting milestone in Red Bank's downtown revitalization journey.
 The day began with a walking tour of downtown, where committee members, project partners, and City staff had the opportunity to visit with local business owners and experience firsthand the strengths, opportunities, and unique character that make our downtown special.
 A special thank you to All About the Bride & Ivory HydroSpa, Vintage and More, Capitol Barbershop, and Bread and Butter for taking the time to visit with our group, provide business tours, and share your unique perspectives on doing business in Downtown Red Bank. Your insight and willingness to engage in the planning process will help shape the future of our downtown.
 Following the tour, the committee participated in a collaborative SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) analysis, identifying priorities, opportunities, and the next steps that will help shape a vibrant, welcoming, and economically resilient downtown.
 This first official meeting represents the beginning of an exciting two-year journey that will build upon community input, strategic planning, and strong partnerships to create a shared vision for Downtown Red Bank.
 A special thank you to The Spritzeria for graciously hosting lunch and providing the perfect venue for the SWOT workshop. Your hospitality and investment in Downtown Red Bank are greatly appreciated.
 We would also like to extend our sincere appreciation to Frank Clark with the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development for his leadership, guidance, and commitment to helping communities like Red Bank build stronger, more vibrant downtowns. Your expertise and support are invaluable as we begin this transformative process.
 Finally, thank you to each member of the Tennessee Downtowns Steering Committee for your willingness to serve and invest your time, ideas, and passion into Red Bank's future. Together, we're laying out the foundation for a downtown that reflects our community's character while creating new opportunities for residents, businesses, and visitors alike.
 Stay tuned as we continue sharing updates throughout this exciting journey!
 #RedBankTN #TNDowntowns #DowntownRedBank #CommunityDevelopment #MainStreet #DowntownRevitalization #TNECD #BuildingCommunity

items.content_text: A family lost their pet in an overnight fire in St. Elmo. At 1:06 AM on 8/3/26, Red Shift companies responded to the 4600 block of Florida Avenue on a reported residential fire. Engine 14 arrived on scene and found heavy fire on the front porch and in the front bedroom of the home. Firefighters began fire attack and conducted searches of the residence, recovering an unresponsive dog. CPR was conducted on the scene by CFD personnel, but the dog did not survive. Crews knocked down fire on the front porch and in the front bedroom and then extinguished hot spots. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

items.content_text:
Know When to Stop for School Buses. It’s the Law! Every driver plays a role in keeping our students safe! 🚍
 • Any road without a median: All lanes of traffic in both directions MUST stop when the bus’s stop arm is extended and red lights are flashing.
 • Divided highway with a median or physical barrier: Only the traffic traveling in the same direction as the bus must stop. Vehicles traveling in the opposite direction must proceed with caution.
 Failing to stop for a school bus is not only dangerous, but also illegal and can result in the serious injury or death of a child. Please slow down, stay alert, and help ensure that every child makes it to and from school safely.

Andy Burnham's move from Mayor of Greater Manchester to Prime Minister has been widely portrayed as unprecedented in British politics. Yet, as LSE Cities Senior Policy Fellow Catarina Heeckt argues, the journey from city hall to national leadership is a familiar one across Europe. What makes Burnham's rise distinctive is not the pathway itself, but the devolution agenda he brings with him. 

Drawing on examples from across Europe, this blog post challenges the idea that Burnham's rise is exceptional. Instead, it shows how city leadership has often provided a route to national office, and why Burnham's devolution agenda may prove more significant than his political trajectory itself. 

Read Catarina's post here: https://lnkd.in/dRiNCKdZ

items.content_text:
Responsible Business Conduct (RBC) means aligning businesses and investment operations with the needs of society, today and in the future. 
 7 out of 10 of the largest listed companies in the world have committed to at least one responsible business issue such as reducing pollution or fighting corruption. 
 The challenge now is turning commitments into action. 
 The #OECD Responsible Business Outlook provides a first global assessment of how responsible business conduct (RBC) is being taken up in companies and government policies. 
 The report finds that: 
 ➡️ A large share of companies have designed policies and management systems to implement RBC (45% of reported practices), but fewer actually identify (25%) and address the impacts of their operations (less than 20%).   
 ➡️ The uptake of due diligence practices is most comprehensive in Europe, Developed Asia-Pacific and Latin America 
 ➡️ They are least comprehensive in China, the Middle East and Africa. 
 How can governments help companies turn their commitments into action? 
 Find out in the full report: https://brnw.ch/21x4Dac
 #OECDResponsibleBusinessConduct

 The report also highlights practical ways government and non-government actors can work together to boost opportunities and spaces for connection within communities through food-related activities.

Bacon is more than breakfast. 🥓 
 In his new book, American Bacon: The History of a Food Phenomenon, UTC history professor Dr. Mark Johnson explores how one familiar food tells a much larger story about American culture, identity, race, labor and changing attitudes toward health and tradition.
 From centuries-old food traditions to today's bacon craze, Johnson's research reveals how history can be found in the everyday things we often take for granted.
